text:
riley: FYI support just escalated a latency spike tied to our 4.0.1 canary (20% traffic). Customer reports p95 for short completions went from ~120ms -> ~700ms. No error rate increase, just tail latency.

taylor: Which customer and which model variant? Any regional skew?

riley: Customer 'NimbusCorp' using hosted API, mostly short prompts (~<=64 tokens). Affected across us-west and eu-west. p50 stable.

jamal: I quickly checked the canary dashboard: https://graf.redwood.internal/d/rt-canary/4.0.1 7-day view  p99 in eu-west spiked to ~1.4s after 4.0.1 ramp. GPU utilization normal. Memory ok.

priya: Can you paste the exact repro request? We need to run an instrumented trace.

riley: Repro (sanitized):

```
POST /v1/completions
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "rt-4.0.1",
  "prompt": "Explain: binary search in 3 lines",
  "max_tokens": 32
}
```

jamal: Ran against canary pool: p95 ~680ms. Baseline (4.0.0) p95 ~115ms.

perf-bot: perf-alert: p95_delta > 3x baseline for model rt-4.0.1 in eu-west (last 10m).

priya: Start a trace with ?debug=trace on internal endpoint and paste id. Also collect kernel selection logs and batching traces.

jamal: Trace id trace-4k-009. Quick summary: several requests hit 'dynamic-batched-kernel' path that allocates per-invocation and triggers small JIT compilations ~250ms. Also saw more frequent 'small-batch' schedule delays (queueing 10-30ms) due to changed batching heuristic.

riley: Where did the change come from in 4.0.1? We had two main changes: batching-window policy tweak and kernel auto-selector overhaul. Candidate root causes.

priya: My hunch is the selector change caused more JITs because it's picking fine-grained kernel configs per seq_len+quant which we didn't prewarm. The batching tweak could amplify effects for bursty mobile traffic.

infra-bot: deploy-canary: rollout 4.0.1 -> canary started at 2026-03-15T05:12:00Z rolling to 20% pools.

jamal: Quick prom I used for p95 by pool:

```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inf_latency_bucket{service=\"runtime\",version=\"4.0.1\"}[2m])) by (le, pool))
```

jamal: Also grep'd kernel logs: lots of entries like: `kernel_jit: compiling fused_attn_v3 for seq=16 quant=int4` around the time spikes begin.

riley: Support asked for mitigation ASAP. Proposed immediate steps: 1) Halt further canary ramp, 2) Move affected customers off canary (pin to 4.0.0), 3) Flip feature flag disabling JIT fallback in kernel selector, 4) Revert batching-window tweak if toggling selector isn't enough.

priya: Agreed. I'm a bit worried about full revert without root cause. Let's toggle selector JIT fallback first and monitor. Also prepare a quick CI prebuild to ensure common seq_len/quant combos are precompiled before re-enabling.

support-bot: Opening support ticket SUP-912 for NimbusCorp. Offering to route traffic to stable runtime and update when fixed.

jamal: Action: paused canary rollout (no further hosts). Pinning NimbusCorp to 4.0.0 pool now.

infra-bot: action: kernelselector.jit_fallback=false applied to canary agents (job id: runtime-canary-flags-421).

jamal: After flag flip, reran repro against canary. p95 dropped from ~680ms -> ~140ms within 3 minutes. p99 also recovered.

riley: Customer confirmed improvement in last 2 min. Nice. We'll keep them pinned and keep canary frozen.

priya: Next: jamal to bisect kernel-selector changes to find the exact commit that added the JIT fallback. I'll add a temporary CI job that runs kernel prebuild for seq lengths [1,4,8,16,32,64] and quant modes [int8,int4]. If prebuild fails or missing combos found, we know we missed targets.

jamal: Starting git bisect now on runtime repo, focusing on kernel-selector PRs + batching heuristics around the 4.0.1 merge window. ETA 3-4 hours to narrow down.

riley: Ops action items: add a 'burst-mobile' synthetic test in canary perf tests that sends small, bursty requests (single-connection, low token counts) to catch regressions like this. Also add automated alert when p95 for canary > baseline_p95 * 2 for 5min.

support-bot: NimbusCorp updated: your traffic is on stable runtime, we're monitoring. Ticket SUP-912.

perf-bot: followup: create ticket infra#1402 for kernel prebuild CI job.

priya: If bisect shows selector is the culprit, options: - revert selector change, - keep selector but remove JIT fallback and force prebuild matrix, - optimize JIT path to reduce cold compile time. We should prefer prebuild + disable fallback for short term.

jamal: Found offending commit: "selector: enable finer-grained kernel selection" which introduced fallback-to-jit for unmatched configs. I'll prepare PR to remove fallback and add explicit prebuild step in buildkite.

riley: Plan: keep canary frozen at 20% with JIT fallback off, re-run prebuild CI, then re-enable selector if prebuild covers combos. If re-enable causes no regressions in 30m synthetic test, we'll slowly resume rollout.

priya: Also add to PR checklist: "Did you run kernel prebuild matrix for common seq lenses?" and require perf approval for selector changes.

jamal: Pushing the PR now. Will link when ready.

riley: Thanks. Leaving thread open until PR merges and canary resumes. Good work everyone.

infra-bot: reminder: create follow-up infra ticket infra#1402 for kernel prebuild job.

support-bot: Closing loop with NimbusCorp for now; will reopen if any regressions.

riley: Closing note: handled without full rollback by toggling flag + customer pin. Postmortem to include improved canary synthetics, CI prebuild, and PR checklist updates.
